Black Swan Student Society

Combining rigorous research, probabilistic thinking, and diverse perspectives to uncover insights and identify opportunities in prediction markets.

Who we are

Founded in 2026, Black Swan is Bocconi University’s first student society dedicated to prediction markets. We bring together independent thinkers to challenge consensus, assess probabilities and identify market inefficiencies through rigorous research and disciplined analysis.

Explore Who We Are
Development

Invested in Your Growth

Build your analytical skills through practical research, with experienced students offering guidance on CVs, internships and recruitment. Publish under your own name and build a body of work that demonstrates your capabilities.

Community

Diverse Perspectives. Shared Ambition.

Join 60+ members across five specialised divisions, brought together by intellectual curiosity. Exchange ideas with traders, researchers and industry professionals, and build lasting relationships through regular society events and informal gatherings.

Ownership

Help Shape What Comes Next

Founded in 2026, Black Swan is still taking shape. Members have the opportunity to lead new initiatives, influence our research agenda and help define the future of Bocconi’s first prediction market society.

Methodology

How the numbers on this page are calculated.

Net PnL
Realised and unrealised profit or loss across all positions, marked to the last traded price and reported before costs.
Hit rate
The share of resolved calls in which the outcome we assigned the higher probability to occurred.
Brier score
The mean squared difference between our stated probability and the outcome (1 or 0). A perfect forecaster scores 0; always guessing 50% scores 0.25.
Log loss
The average negative log-likelihood of our forecasts. It rewards calibrated confidence and penalises confident misses heavily.
Edge at entry
Our probability minus the market-implied probability at the time a position is opened, in percentage points.
Sharpe ratio
Average period return divided by its standard deviation, annualised. Reported once enough history exists to be meaningful.
Max drawdown
The largest fall in cumulative PnL from a previous peak, in the reporting currency.

Figures will be updated monthly and reported before costs. Positions are sized according to the society’s internal guidelines. Past performance, once reported, is no guarantee of future results; nothing on this page is investment advice.

Black Swan Student Society

Black Swan is promoted and run by students of Bocconi University. Founded in 2026, it is Bocconi’s first student society dedicated to prediction markets.

5

Divisions

Business & Finance, Economics & Politics, Cross‑Domain, Market Studies and Algorithmic Development, each producing research on a distinct set of markets.

60+

Members

A board of 16 and 49 analysts, drawn from undergraduate and graduate programmes across the university.

Frequently asked questions

Other questions? Write to as.blackswan@unibocconi.it

Who can apply?

Black Swan is open to undergraduate and graduate students at Bocconi University, from any degree programme and year of study.

Do I need experience with prediction markets?

No. We value curiosity, rigour and independent thinking over prior experience. Members learn the mechanics of prediction markets through their division’s work.

Can I apply to more than one division?

You indicate a first and second preference on the application form. Where possible, we place candidates in their first choice.

When does the next round open?

The next application round opens in January. It will be announced on this page and on our Instagram.

Who can I contact with questions?

Write to us at as.blackswan@unibocconi.it and a member of the board will get back to you.

Home/Divisions & Performance/Business & Finance

Division 01 · Investment research

Business & Finance

Earnings|Industry rankings|M&A

2 division heads|17 analysts|0 published reports

On this page

Overview

The Business & Finance Division applies fundamental analysis and probabilistic modelling to prediction markets surrounding corporate performance and transactions. Our analysts examine the commercial, financial and strategic forces behind each event, translating company research into explicit forecasts. We seek to identify where market expectations diverge from the evidence, whether through an overlooked operating driver, an optimistic timetable or a misinterpretation of transaction terms.

Our approach combines bottom-up research with disciplined scrutiny of market expectations. Drawing on financial statements, company disclosures, industry data and historical precedents, teams develop scenarios, assess their likelihood and test the assumptions that determine their conclusions. Each investment thesis must articulate a precise disagreement with the prevailing price, withstand a credible counterargument and identify the developments that would warrant revision.

Home/Divisions & Performance/Economics & Politics

Division 02 · Investment research

Economics & Politics

Central banks|Macro data|Elections & policy

1 division head|16 analysts|0 published reports

On this page

Overview

The Economics & Politics Division applies macroeconomic analysis and probabilistic modelling to prediction markets surrounding monetary policy, economic data and political outcomes. Our analysts study central bank decisions, inflation and labour-market releases, elections, legislation, trade policy and geopolitical developments, translating that research into explicit forecasts. We seek to identify where market expectations diverge from the evidence, whether through a misread policy reaction function, an overreaction to a single poll or a misunderstanding of how a contract resolves.

Our approach combines top-down analysis with close attention to the data that drives each outcome. Drawing on official statistics, central bank communication, polling, historical precedents and institutional rules, teams build scenarios, weigh them against forecasts and survey data, and track how markets absorb new information. Each thesis must state a precise disagreement with the prevailing price, withstand a credible counterargument and identify the releases or events that would warrant revision.

Home/Divisions & Performance/Cross-Domain

Division 03 · Investment research

Cross-Domain

Crypto|Weather|Appearances & mentions

1 division head|6 analysts|0 published reports

On this page

Overview

The Cross-Domain Division covers prediction markets outside traditional finance, from cryptocurrency prices and weather outcomes to public appearances and mention markets. Our analysts bring quantitative methods and domain-specific research to questions where information is fragmented and participants rely on very different sources. We seek to identify where market expectations diverge from the evidence, whether through a poorly calibrated volatility assumption, an overlooked forecast model or a misreading of what counts towards resolution.

Our approach adapts to the structure of each market. For price-based contracts, teams model the distribution of outcomes using volatility, historical behaviour and current market conditions; for weather and event markets, they compare forecasts and base rates across independent sources; for mention and appearance markets, they study schedules, precedents and the precise wording of the resolution criteria. Each thesis must state where and why our probability differs from the market, withstand a credible counterargument and identify what would change our view.

Home/Divisions & Performance/Market Studies

Division 04 · Markets & models

Market Studies

Closed markets|Statistical analysis|Price drivers

2 division heads|4 analysts|0 published reports

On this page

Overview

The Market Studies Division examines prediction markets themselves: how prices form, how quickly they absorb new information and how accurate they prove once questions resolve. Rather than taking positions on individual events, our analysts study the behaviour of markets across many contracts, producing reports and statistical research on what closed markets reveal about calibration, liquidity and the drivers of price movements.

Our approach is empirical. Teams assemble data on resolved markets, define testable hypotheses and apply statistical methods to measure accuracy, bias and reaction to news, with careful attention to sample selection, contract design and trading conditions. Findings are reviewed critically before publication, and the patterns they uncover inform the research of the other divisions and the models built by Algorithmic Development.

Home/Divisions & Performance/Algorithmic Development

Division 05 · Markets & models

Algorithmic Development

Statistical models|Backtesting|Systematic trading

1 division head|6 analysts|0 published reports

On this page

Overview

The Algorithmic Development Division builds and evaluates statistical models and systematic strategies for prediction markets. Our analysts turn research ideas into testable rules, using quantitative methods to search for persistent sources of edge and to measure whether they survive realistic trading conditions.

Our approach follows a disciplined research process. Each strategy begins with a clear hypothesis, is developed on historical data and is tested out of sample, with explicit treatment of transaction costs, liquidity, position sizing and the risk of overfitting. Models are documented so that their assumptions can be scrutinised, and their live performance is compared against backtested expectations to decide whether they should be refined, scaled or retired.

Introduction

Black Swan is Bocconi’s first student society dedicated to prediction markets. With over 60 members across five divisions, we bring together undergraduate and graduate students interested in how markets form expectations—and where those expectations may be wrong.

Our work combines fundamental research, statistical analysis and debate. Members investigate real-world events, develop independent forecasts and compare their conclusions with market prices.

Our Mission

We aim to produce thoughtful, accessible research while helping members develop practical analytical skills and lasting relationships.

Prediction markets give our work a clear focus: what will happen, by when, and with what probability? Answering those questions requires members to weigh evidence, challenge assumptions and explain their reasoning. Reviewing the outcomes then gives them an opportunity to learn from both good judgments and mistakes.

Our Story

Our name takes inspiration from Nassim Nicholas Taleb’s The Black Swan, which examines rare, consequential events that fall outside conventional expectations and often seem explainable only afterwards.

For us, the name is a reminder to question certainty, consider overlooked possibilities and recognise the limits of our knowledge. We do not claim that every surprise can be predicted. We believe that thinking carefully about uncertainty leads to better questions and better decisions.

Black Swan grew from a shared interest in exploring these ideas through prediction markets. After gathering student signatures and presenting the society to the university, we established a community where students could research, discuss and test their views together.

Invested in Your Growth

Black Swan gives members the opportunity to develop research they can put their names to and confidently discuss. Working alongside students with different experience and interests helps them strengthen their analysis, communicate clearly and learn from one another.

More experienced members also offer support with CVs, internships and recruiting. Alongside research, professional events and social activities help turn the society into a community.

We are still building Black Swan. Members have the opportunity to propose projects, develop new initiatives and shape what the society becomes.

Home/Who we are/Philosophy and process

Who we are

Philosophy and process

On this page

Philosophy

Black Swan combines fundamental research, quantitative analysis and independent judgment to explore prediction markets. Across our five divisions, we investigate real-world events, study how markets form expectations and develop methods for identifying where prices may be wrong.

Our approach rests on independent judgment and intellectual rigour. Before challenging a market price or proposing an explanation, members establish the strongest alternative interpretation. Conclusions must follow from evidence, with a clear distinction between observed facts, modelling assumptions and forecasts.

We recognise that uncertainty cannot be eliminated. Our objective is to assess it carefully, communicate it clearly and revise our conclusions when the evidence changes. We evaluate research through the quality and consistency of its reasoning, recognising that individual outcomes do not necessarily validate or invalidate the underlying approach.

Process

  1. 01

    Working with their division heads, members develop projects suited to their interests and expertise. Teams combine undergraduate and graduate students from different academic backgrounds, bringing together subject knowledge, analytical skills and varied perspectives.

  2. 02

    Each project begins with a precise research question and an appropriate analytical framework. For event research, this means defining the outcome, deadline and contractual resolution criteria. For market studies and algorithm development, it means establishing a testable hypothesis, identifying suitable data and specifying how results will be evaluated.

  3. 03

    Teams then investigate the drivers of the outcome or behaviour under study. Methods may include primary-source research, economic and financial modelling, historical comparisons, statistical inference and backtesting. The choice of method follows the question, with assumptions and limitations made explicit.

  4. 04

    Findings are subjected to scenario analysis, sensitivity testing and critical review. Members consider competing explanations, assess the reliability of their evidence and examine whether conclusions remain credible under alternative assumptions. Where research informs a trading strategy, the analysis also accounts for execution costs, liquidity and the risk of overfitting historical data.

  5. 05

    Projects culminate in reports, presentations or research tools that make the evidence, methodology and conclusions open to scrutiny. Teams monitor subsequent developments and revisit their findings to improve both their judgments and their methods.

Research and Development

Our five divisions provide complementary approaches to prediction markets. Economics & Politics, Business & Finance and Cross-Domain develop research on events within their respective fields. Market Studies examines price formation, information processing and market behaviour, while Algorithm Development builds and evaluates statistical models and systematic strategies.

Collaboration between divisions connects detailed subject knowledge with broader empirical analysis. Event research can generate hypotheses for testing across markets, while quantitative findings can reveal patterns that warrant deeper investigation.

Through collaborative projects, structured feedback and published research, members develop practical capabilities in analysis, modelling, programming and communication. We aim to produce work that contributes to a better understanding of prediction markets while giving members a rigorous foundation for further study and professional practice.

Home/Who we are/Our values

Who we are

Our values

The principles behind how we research, debate and build the society together.

Initiative|Community|Integrity|Growth and Development

01

Initiative

Build what isn’t here yet.

We value initiative because Black Swan is new. Founded in 2026, the society has no long-established playbook to follow: its research agenda, events and traditions are being created by the members who step forward and take ownership. We give members room to pitch projects, propose events and lead new initiatives, and we back good ideas with the time and support needed to make them happen.

02

Community

Better judgments are made together.

We value community because good forecasting is rarely a solo effort. Our best work comes from people who trust each other enough to share unfinished ideas, question each other’s reasoning and change their minds in the open. We bring members together through joint projects, peer mentorship, professional events and informal gatherings, so that everyone knows the people they work alongside.

03

Integrity

Say what you think, and show how you got there.

We value integrity because a forecast is only useful if it is honest. Overstating confidence, hiding assumptions or explaining away a poor call undermines both the research and the trust placed in it. We separate evidence from assumption, credit the work of others and review our calls openly, including the ones that went against us.

04

Growth and Development

Leave sharper than you arrived.

We have a strong commitment to growth and development because a student society should leave its members more capable than it found them. Prediction markets provide constant, honest feedback, which makes them an exceptional place to learn. Experienced members mentor newer ones, feedback is specific and constructive, and members publish research under their own names, building a body of work that shows their progress.

Diversity

Diversity

Independent views make better forecasts.

Black Swan believes diversity of thought is essential to sound research and well-functioning prediction markets. The wisdom of a crowd depends on the independence of its judgments: when participants rely on the same sources, assumptions and methods, their agreement can reinforce a shared bias rather than reflect stronger evidence.

We therefore seek students who approach questions differently, bring unfamiliar perspectives and are willing to challenge the prevailing view—including our own. Across Bocconi’s undergraduate and graduate community, we welcome members of all backgrounds and levels of experience.

Through collaborative research, peer mentorship and open debate, we aim to give every member the confidence and opportunity to contribute an independent voice.

04 / 16

Leadership

Mohammed El-Zein

Senior Advisor

Mohammed (Moe) serves as Senior Advisor to Black Swan’s leadership, supporting the President and division heads on strategic and operational matters. He is a second-year MSc student in Accounting & Financial Management at Bocconi, where he is completing a Double Degree with Grenoble Ecole de Management. He previously studied Quantitative Economics at the University of Konstanz, where he served as a Research Assistant at the Chair of Applied Microeconomics. Having grown up between Germany and Lebanon and studied in France and Italy, he has learned to feel at home wherever the conversation is most interesting. He has gained experience through internships in investment banking at UniCredit in Corporate Structured & Acquisition Finance, in M&A advisory for German Mittelstand companies at Menold Bezler, in the Corporate Bank at Commerzbank, and in the Financial Services Industry practice at Deloitte. At Grenoble, he serves as Programme Representative for all MSc Finance programmes. His interest in how global events move markets, and in how people from different backgrounds reach better decisions together, drew him to Black Swan. Outside university, he enjoys exploring new coffee shops and restaurants, playing padel, and spending time with friends and family.

Divisions

Niklas Ondruch

Co-Head of Business & Finance

Niklas (Niki) co-leads Black Swan’s Business and Finance Division and is a second-year International Economics and Finance student at Bocconi. Raised in London by French and German parents, he first explored investing at 14 through a virtual trading portfolio. He has since gained experience through internships in credit investing at hedge fund Sternlight Capital Partners, equity research at Astellon Capital Partners – a former hedge fund turned family office – and Sales and Trading at Marex Group. His interest in behavioural economics and how markets bring together different perspectives inspired him to help establish Black Swan. Outside university, he enjoys football, basketball, chess and training for Ironman triathlons.

Divisions

Loyd Hegarty

Co-Head of Business & Finance

Loyd co-leads Black Swan’s Business and Finance Division and is a second-year International Economics and Finance student at Bocconi. With a French-British background and an education in Romania, he developed an interest in financial markets that led him to internships in Global Markets at Société Générale in Paris. He has also explored company valuation through equity research at Minerva Investment Management Society and merger analysis at Bocconi’s Distressed Investing and Restructuring Club. At Black Swan, he aims to bring these perspectives together, helping analysts connect financial research with market expectations to develop informed views on prediction markets. Outside university, he enjoys football and going to the gym.

Media, Operations & Recruitment

Adrian Tsonev

Head of Recruitment

Adrian (Adi) Tsonev leads Black Swan’s Market Updates and Career Guidance sector and is a second-year International Economics and Finance student at Bocconi. Raised in London by Bulgarian parents, he first gained an interest in finance when he pursued an internship at Ares Management during high school. Since then, he has gained experience in high-yield credit trading during the Barings Spring Week, Sales and Trading during the Goldman Sachs Insight Program, and long/short credit trading at hedge fund Sternlight Capital Partners. His strong interest in financial markets and finding investment opportunities within them inspired him to help establish Black Swan. Outside university, he enjoys playing rugby, football, tennis and piano.
